findings.where: r5core.py:657-664 (duty), 712-737 (progress), 674-687 with r5lib.py:396-410 (clearance a); rule text r5core.py:127-164; against STAGE2_TRACKB_PLAN.md W2, W3, W5 (worktree /home/user/mesozoic-wt/prereg-b, commit 103bf35)
findings.problem: The reward the env computes is not the committed rule text's in two terms, and reads two more in its own way. (1) duty: W2 says "Stage 1's (W3 for the band)"; the code charges a foot only where the reference's own contact share over the same stride lies inside the band. (2) progress: W5 fixes min(1, max(0, 1 - v_bar / (1.05 v_cmd)) / 0.10); the code computes (v_ref_bar - v_bar) / (1.05 v_cmd), with v_ref_bar the same mean of the reference's own CoM speed, restarted at each periodic walking segment. (3) clearance (a) times the swing by the planned length of the reference's swing in progress, on the reference clock. (4) foot, head, heading, tilt and tracking read positions as of the last physics step's start, not the env step's end (said in the module docstring only). The builder declares 1-3 in REWARD_RULE and READINGS, but the committed W2/W3/W5 still hold the literal formulas, and W2's Check compares only weights and scales, so a run.json would pass it with another formula. A run launched like this breaks a rule fixed before the runs.
findings.evidence: My own kinematic computation on Stage 1's stock references (scratch rv_ref.py and an inline script; no episode): the literal texts cannot hold together with W1 ("a playback scores every penalty 0"). W5's literal progress on the reference's own CoM speed: 75-M-H-10 nominal max 0.29-0.30, mean 0.051-0.056 (CoM speed 0.201-0.317 m/s inside a stride against 0.243); brisk max 0.17-0.19; 60-N-T-10 nominal max 0.27-0.29. W2's literal duty on the reference's own contacts: charged on 84 of 919 env steps of the S1 walk task (26 % of the start's steps and 6 % of the stop's, up to 1.0; task mean 0.088) and on 147 of 1,480 of the brisk task. So the builder's readings are defensible, but they are the lead's to rule. Positions: at one perturbed walking state the foot term reads 0.9810 as coded and 0.9724 on the pose at the step's end.
findings.fix: Before state B the lead rules. Recommended, with no code change: amend STAGE2_TRACKB_PLAN.md with the tag [lead, before any Track B run]: W2's duty row gets "a foot is read only where the reference's own share over the same stride lies inside the band"; W5's progress becomes min(1, max(0, (v_ref_bar - v_bar) / (1.05 v_cmd)) / 0.10) with v_ref_bar defined as in r5core.REWARD_RULE and "restarted at the segment's first frame, read after one stride"; W3 (a) names the planned length of the reference's swing in progress, on the reference clock; W1 says positions are those of the last physics step's start. Add that last sentence to r5core.REWARD_RULE too, and extend W2's Check to equality of the env description's reward_rule text. If the lead refuses a reading, revert it at the lines named.

findings.where: r5lib.py:783 (a start's or change's command is gait b's from its first frame), 375-377 and 804-805 (the commanded heading is the integral of that w); read at r5core.py:450-452 (heading input) and 700-703 (heading penalty)
findings.problem: In the turn-in-place tasks (T1 inplace_left, inplace_right) the commanded heading runs away from the reference. The start into the turn commands 0.5 rad/s from its first frame (rule E4, followed to the letter) while the reference ramps its yaw rate up from rest, so the reference's own yaw stays behind the commanded heading through the whole periodic part and only catches up in the stop. The heading penalty then charges the reference itself and the actor's heading input is saturated: rule W1 (a playback scores every penalty 0) is false for these tasks, and the policy is paid to turn away from the reference it imitates. No test covers it: S1_TASKS has no turn in place and the playback tests run brisk and stop only. The same mechanism gives a smaller transient in the finite turns, where a rectangular pulse meets a ramped reference.
findings.evidence: Kinematic, Stage 1's stock arrays, plan start_in_place_0.50_left, in_place_0.50_left x 3, stop_in_place_0.50_left through lib.from_plan (rv_ref.py): the reference's yaw less the commanded heading is -71.6 deg at the periodic segment's first and last frame on 75-M-H-10 (-64.3 deg on 60-N-T-10) and 0.0 at the plan's end; mirrored for right. In the env with the zero action on that plan (S1 view, hard floor, nominal plant; the robot follows the reference: joint term 1.000, no fall): heading penalty mean 0.73, at 1.0 on 69 % of the env steps, heading input at -2 on 51 % (75 cm); 0.73, 68 %, 49 % (60 cm). Finite turns, computed and not measured (S1 has none): w0 x ramp / 2 with setio.RAMP_S 0.375 s is 8.4 deg at pi/4 rad/s (penalty 0.32 during the turn) and 10.7 deg at 1.0 rad/s (0.45).
findings.fix: Needs one sentence of the lead in E4, before state B (r5lib.py enters the rows' sources). Proposed: inside a finite segment that is no finite turn and that enters or leaves a gait with a yaw rate, the command stays E4's but the commanded heading follows the reference's own yaw: in r5lib._tables record the segment's yaw gain from seg.info["yaw"] and let Script.heading return heading0 + (track.info(t) yaw - yaw at the segment's t0) there, the next segment's heading0 being its value at the segment's end (lines 375-377, 804-805). Add an in-place plan on S1 arrays to test_a_playback_scores_imitation_one_and_every_penalty_zero. For the finite turns either accept the transient in words in W1/W5, or have G9-ref (f) record each task script's playback penalties on the look set.

findings.problem: The env refuses to build when the set's latest freeze is not the one in its config. Rule K4 (and design 3.6) accepts a later freeze when every used file's and entry's hash and the resolved task table are unchanged. The run's settings hold env_configs[] with set_freeze, and changed settings are always refused, so a resume must build its envs from the stored configs: after any later freeze of that set and body those are refused by the env itself, and a config carrying the new hash is no longer equal to the stored one. K4's accepted case cannot be reached. A local run (M6, the 75 cm run) that meets a later freeze cannot be resumed without a code change.
findings.evidence: Synthetic set in my scratch directory (the tests' own make_t0 fixture, Stage 1 arrays, kinematic only): R5Env(R5Config(set="T0", set_freeze=<freeze 0's manifest sha256>)) builds. After appending freeze 1 (the same entries plus one new record) the same config raises InputError "the set's freeze is 78feee62ecb4..., the settings name 60257508a6fe...". With the new hash in the config the env builds and describe()["inputs"]["files"] and ["tasks"] are unchanged, but the config differs from the stored one. No test of the package builds an env with set_freeze set and then freezes again.
findings.fix: At r5env.py:211-214 accept cfg.set_freeze when it is the manifest_sha256 of any freeze in the set's set.json (setio.load(dir)["set.json"]["freezes"]) and refuse only a hash the set never had. Keep cfg.set_freeze as "the freeze the run started on" (design 3.2) and add set_freeze_now = {index, manifest_sha256} to describe(), so the trainer records both indices and applies K4's comparison on describe()["inputs"]["files"] and ["tasks"], which already hold the used files' hashes and the resolved table. Add a test on the synthetic set: later freeze with unchanged files builds; an unknown hash is refused.

findings.where: r5core.py:179 (JAW_OPEN_RAD = (0.3, 0.6), used by HeadScript.drawn and HeadScript.fixed), r5core.py:704-705 (range term) with r5lib.py:323-328 (required margin)
findings.problem: On the -X bodies the jaw's range is [0, 0.6] rad and the head command opens it to 0.3-0.6 rad (rules E5, J4). A jaw that sits exactly on its commanded opening above 0.5 rad is inside the 0.10 rad margin of its upper limit. In training, the range penalty charges obeying the command (W5's "the reference itself scores zero" fails with a head command), which pays the policy to hold the jaw back. On the bar, panels._base reads joint_margins over every joint with required 0.10 rad, so an R5G episode under head script H1 (one jaw event always present) fails joint_range by the script alone whenever the target exceeds 0.5 rad: a third of the episodes of the "cost of using the head" reading, whatever the policy does.
findings.evidence: Both -X plants built here: jaw range 0.0 to 0.6, rest end the lower one; neck_yaw -0.6 to 0.6; required margin 0.10 for both in the walk script. Range term with every joint on its commanded target: jaw 0.45 gives 0.000; jaw 0.60 gives 1.000 (margin 0.0000, required 0.1000); penalty above 0 from 0.50 rad and 1.0 from 0.52 rad, so 33 % and 27 % of jaw events drawn uniform on 0.3-0.6. Neck yaw at +-0.5 leaves margin 0.1000 exactly, so any overshoot there is charged too. The bar's reading: panels.py:1067-1069 and 1087 (joint_shortfall_rad <= 0), bar.py:1001.
findings.fix: Put to the lead before state B, with these numbers (ruling 7 accepted H1's numbers as drafted, without them): open the jaw to at most its range less the bar's margin and a tracking allowance, for example JAW_OPEN_RAD = (0.3, 0.45) and the gaze target on +-0.45 rad, in r5core.py:176-181 and in E5 and J4. bar.py cannot be edited after state A, so the script's numbers are the place. Then add a test on both -X bodies: a playback with HeadScript events at their extremes scores range 0, and its joint margins meet the bar's 0.10 rad.

findings.where: r5env.py:263-266 (_mid) and 426-434 (the queue refill, only when k > 0); r5core.py:264-275 (reset_at)
findings.problem: At a mid-task start the estimator's first reading (foot loads, accelerometer, contact flags) is taken from Plant.set_state's forward pass, which runs with the servos at their home targets while the pose is mid-stride. For k > 0 the env then sets the delayed reference command and calls mj_forward, which corrects the plant's sensordata but not the estimator. For k = 0 nothing is corrected, and Core.begin takes its first contact flags from the same pass. Pose, velocity, clock and queue are consistent; the first observation's foot_load block and the estimator's first contact decision are not.
findings.evidence: 60 mid starts per delay on 75-M-H-10 (S1 view, nominal plant): the reset observation's foot_load averages 1.21 body weights, up to 4.66, and 60 % of resets show a foot over 2 BW, for k = 0 and for k = 5. The plant's own loads at reset average 0.35 (max 1.56) for k = 5, and one env step later the input averages 0.55-0.58 (max 1.5-1.6); stance starts give 0.41 (max 0.98). With the reference's own command the loads at the same states are 0.5-1.3 BW.
findings.fix: In reset step 12, for every mid start, k = 0 included: set p.d.ctrl to the zero-action command of the physics step before the start (queue[0] when k > 0, else self._zero_ctrl(tk, max(t_start - step, 0))), call mujoco.mj_forward, then give the estimator a reading from that pass: tk.est.reset(p.d.qpos.copy(), p.d.qvel.copy(), tk.sensors.read()), and call core.begin after it. Mid starts are not part of G8a, so no gate moves; the mid-start tests' expected digests do.

findings.where: r5core.py:660 (v_cmd < duty_slow_below_m_s), fed by r5lib.py:759 (the entry's speed_m_s)
findings.problem: W3's duty band switches at a commanded target speed of 0.30 m/s, and one rung of the ladder is exactly 0.30. The code compares the entry's float speed_m_s with <. The bar takes a rung's target from its name (BarPlanner.speed). If the v0.3 entry holds 0.29999999999999993 (a stride over a period), that rung trains under 0.55-0.72 while the bar judges it under 0.55-0.65.
findings.evidence: Reading only: the look sets are not built. Stage 1's entries hold computed speeds (nominal 0.24306007460404672).
findings.fix: Read the band from the named target: in r5lib._tables keep s.v_target = setio.parse_name(name)["speed_m_s"] (None: the entry's speed_m_s), expose it (Script.target_speed), and compare that at r5core.py:660. A test with an entry whose speed_m_s is 0.30 - 1e-16 under the name v0.3.

findings.problem: The loop that maps the uniform draw onto the spans can leave u a rounding step above the last span's length, and min(a + u, b) then returns b. In the stop and start_stop tasks the last span ends at a hold's first instant, where Script.start_state raises ValueError ("lies in a hold"), which would end a training worker.
findings.evidence: Reading only; the chance is of the order of 1e-16 per reset and 400 resets here never met it. The span ends are the hold's t0 on the S1 stop task: spans (0.2, 5.678), (5.678, 7.949), (7.949, 13.627) with the hold from 13.627.
findings.fix: Clamp inside the span: t = a + min(u, b - a), and if t >= b: t = float(np.nextafter(b, a)), before script.start_state(t).

verdict: The env does what gate G8a and design D16 need, and I found no defect in its physics path; it should not go to state B until the lead has ruled on one blocker and three major findings. Checked with my own scripts on Stage 1's stock references only (S1 view; no Stage 2 set touched, worktree left clean, scratch under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-mesozoic-labs/2dca1c00-13f3-5853-acf6-8c3e3e04feb6/scratchpad/review_wpc_ce/): the zero action is the panels' R0 row bit for bit in 20 episodes and about 135,000 physics steps, at 0 and 10 ms, on 75-M-H-10, 75-M-H-10-X, 60-N-T-10 and 60-N-T-10-X, on walks, turns, pushes, mu 0.54, a carpet fall (row step 2,237, env step 224) and a 60 cm fall, also in a training-config env after randomised episodes with random actions; a stricter digest with warm start, time and applied forces agrees, and residual stays None and rate_factor exactly 1.0 at every env step. An action entry of 1e-6 changes the digest within the first env step. Layouts are 88/130/15 and 102/146/17 (87/129, 101/145 without the heading) with E3's block table, and the observation blocks equal independent readings on a 16-joint env with a head script. Mid-task starts put plant and estimator on the file's frame (rates x 1.05) with Stage 1's noise, the clock on the start time and the delayed commands on the reference's (to 1e-13), never in a hold, about half of non-stand episodes, reproducible from the seed and equal in a fresh env. Twelve consecutive episodes' task, start, factors, push, head events and seeds equal DRAW_ORDER replayed by hand from the seeded generator, on 14 and 16 joints. Trackers, a lazily built plan tracker and its track stay nominal after randomised episodes and the model is restored bit for bit. Six reward terms and the weighted sum match a hand computation, and interference follows W4 (ramp on moving pairs only, termination at two step ends in a row, off for the gates). Four fresh processes (two alike, one with another PYTHONHASHSEED, one with a warm-up history) give identical digests for R5 on hard floor, carpet and 16 joints, for R6 and for 60 cm. R6's span, targets and mid-start history are right. Only the eight owned files changed, with no Stage 1 or round-A file touched, and the builder's four test files pass here (42 passed; 29 passed, 1 skipped). Step rate of one env process, not alone (load average 2.4-3.2 on 4 cores; CPU-time rate within 2 % of wall): hard floor 385 env steps/s at sigma 0.1 and 401 with the zero action; robot_floor_carpet 302 and 413; resident memory 262-265 MB; build 2.1-2.2 s. What stands in the way: the reward departs from the committed W2/W3/W5 text in duty and progress (the literal text contradicts W1, so the rule text should be amended, but that is the lead's ruling); the turn-in-place tasks penalise the reference itself through the commanded heading (zero action: heading penalty at 1.0 on 69 % of the steps); the env refuses the later freeze that K4 accepts; and the jaw command of E5/J4 reaches the jaw's limit, which the range penalty charges and which would fail the bar's joint_range in about a third of R5G episodes.
